title: What skills do you recommend for ChatGPT? For large-scale games?
author: ChocolateTemporary48
selftext:
I am starting development on a space strategy game based on the concept of humanity's role in the Human-Covenant War—specifically, facing an enemy that is technologically and numerically superior, and having to find weaknesses and use ingenuity to survive and counterattack.



I would appreciate recommendations for skills and resources that could make things easier for ChatGPT.

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
I only have a couple skills for code review and flagging problems in sessions. The skills are nice to have, but they solve specific problems that I had. 

Just start anyway. Grab an engine, use Codex + the CLI, and start working on your game. My first prompt to ChatGPT in a game project was “I want to make a game with AI but I don’t know how to do that,” or something like that.

replies.author: ChocolateTemporary48
replies.body:
I looked up various abilities—with the help of ChatGPT, of course. The game is being built in Godot, and well, it's running on SOL 6.1 at Ultra settings.



As for the final size, honestly, I don't know yet; I'm limited by not being able to use MCP properly, since I'm on Windows 10 (my computer isn't compatible with Windows 11).

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body:
MCP is not critical and a lot of people don’t use it. You can do CLI instead. Keep in mind that you can also have GPT write tools for itself to use.

“Ultra” is fun but it a lot of tasks do not benefit from that effort level, and the extra effort often makes your sessions slower. I would start with a lower default level of effort.

comments.author: count023
comments.body:
none, skills basically eat  your tokens for minimal rate of return. Most people have stopped using them because tokens are more important than loquacious monoliths that give no performance gains.

The only skills worth using are publishing ones that are for packaging up your game for whatever platform you're releasing on or issuing a build.

replies.author: ChocolateTemporary48
replies.body: Why do they consume tokens? Shouldn't they make things more efficient and reduce the number of steps involved?

replies.author: count023
replies.body: a lot of stills write massive walls of text to force the AI to give you exact result the skill promises, whereas a simple sentence or two can achieve the same result much more effectively, so you end up spnding 1000 or 5000 tokens with a skill per use, rather than simply 500 tokens writing out a more clear sentence or two describing your requirements.

replies.author: ChocolateTemporary48
replies.body: I understand; I'll be careful with the skills I choose and review the ones I already have.

comments.author: Gigaslavx
comments.body:
Don't think formal education is needed

I say it's all about experience and expertise

1 very important to know what makes games fun which means playing a lot yourself

2 while not knowing how to code all here is what AI is for, you still need to know how to build a game in what order of stages and layers without cutting corners to avoid major rewrites and project abandonments

replies.author: ChocolateTemporary48
replies.body: I was referring to skills for ChatGPT. I have absolutely no idea how to program, so I'm leaving all the hard work to it.

comments.author: MechaLenin111
comments.body: I have a custom skill which is supposed to limit number of tests run in Godot to only essential ones. Honestly, I'm not sure it's worth it, got no good way of measuring the effect.

comments.author: heavy-minium
comments.body:
You need to know what you're gonna work with, only then do skills make sense. Blender? Unity? Godot? Three.js? etc?

Providing a GDD? Or one prompt slop generation? Any target images?

There is so much more to consider.

![gif](giphy|h40jcPnWq7x5buK6Am)

replies.author: ChocolateTemporary48
replies.body: I’m with Godot on this; regarding the prompt, I established an initial plan that I later expanded with ChatGPT's help—basically, the initial prompt consisted of some basic rules and following the plan.
